thread:
maya: FYI eu-west (euw1) external egress link degraded ~30% starting now, saw burst in inference queue

alex: saw it on the p99 dashboards, small-gen routes p99 jumped 1.3s -> ~4.6s :grimacing:

opsbot: Alert: network-egress-euw1 degraded. Rule: queue_length>/v1/generate > 200

jiro: quick baseline numbers to anchor decisions: SLO p99 = 1.5s, current observed p99 ~4.6s, p95 ~1.8s. total throughput approx -18%

maya: I ran a quick deterministic sim to see backlog growth given our admit curve. numbers below. backlog reaches critical in ~10-12m if unchanged.

maya: sim snippet:
```
# sketch sim for backlog tokens
qps = 1100                 # incoming requests/sec
avg_tokens = 30            # avg tokens per request
egress_factor = 0.7        # 30% egress reduction
tokens_per_gpu_sec = 8200
usable_gpus = 38
effective_tp = usable_gpus * tokens_per_gpu_sec * egress_factor
incoming_tokens_sec = qps * avg_tokens
backlog_growth_tokens_per_sec = incoming_tokens_sec - effective_tp
```

jiro: that matches my hand calc. backlog_growth > 0 -> admit curve will delay triggering, so tails get worse before it self-corrects

sam: options we should consider now:
- shift admit curve to reject earlier (ated admit threshold down ~20%)
- reduce batching latency knobs (max_wait) to lower tail at expense of throughput
- failover latency-sensitive tenant traffic to another region (e.g., eu-central)
- temporary capacity bump (add GPUs) in euw1

leah: cost implications quick notes: (1) config change nearly free, (2) tighter max_wait can raise GPU-hours marginally (more smaller batches), (3) cross-region failover adds egress + interconnect cost and potential cold-starts, (4) adding 4 GPUs -> ~96 GPU-hrs/day (estimate)

alex: micro-math: 4 gpus * 24h = 96 gpu-hr. using committed rate ~ $3.50/hr -> ~ $336/day. egress cost for failing over same traffic could be similar depending on bytes/sec and routes

sam: important leaderboard: autoscaler lead time ~10-15m to attach extra gpus (provision + model warmup). If degradation <20m, config/knobs + canary may be faster and less costy

maya: canary plan: push admit curve earlier by 20% and set max_wait 12ms on 10% of traffic. monitor p95/p99 and queue depth for 30m. if p99 stays >2.5s after 30m, escalate to scale +4 gpus and alert customers

opsbot: Deploy OK: admit-curve canary rolled to 10% (maya)

alex: early numbers from canary: p99 -> 2.4s (was 4.6s), p95 -> 1.6s. queue depth on canary reduced ~40% vs baseline. overall cluster still shows higher tails for remaining 90%

jiro: note: reducing max_wait reduces batching latency but may reduce tokens/sec efficiency. we optimised for tail reduction in the canary which is expected tradeoff

leah: for incident notes / chargeback: please include estimated delta: admit-curve change cost delta ~+0.5% GPU-hrs; if we need to scale +4 GPUs for 6 hours -> ~24 GPU-hrs -> ~$84 at committed rate; failover unknown but likely >$100 for short window due to egress and networking

maya: agreed. I've inserted those estimates into the incident doc and pinged finance for visibility. also added a health check to auto-revert canary after 60m if p99 doesn't improve

sam: small reminder: check cold KV cache effect if we add GPUs — model KV warmup might add extra latency initially; factor into the 10-15m warmup time

maya: timeline: keep canary 30m, if p99 <=2.5s then continue roll. if p99 >2.5s after 30m -> scale +4gpus (autoscaler) and send customer notice. I'll update incident channel in 15m

opsbot: Incident logged: network-egress-euw1 degraded. Duration so far: 22m

alex: thanks all — monitoring closely. :thumbsup:
